title: 泊船瓜洲
author: 王安石
intro: Moored on the Yangtze, a statesman looks back toward his home just a few hills away and asks when the moon will light his way back. Famous for one word — 绿, “green”, used as a verb.
analysis: 王安石的家在江宁（今南京），这次他坐船经过长江北岸的瓜洲，停船过夜。前两句写距离：京口和瓜洲只隔着一条长江，从这里到钟山（他家附近的山）也只隔着几座山。家看起来这么近，却回不去。第三句“春风又绿江南岸”最有名，“绿”本来是形容词，这里用作动词，意思是“吹绿了”：春风一吹，江南岸边又变成了一片绿色。传说王安石先后试过“到”“过”“入”“满”等十几个字，最后才定下“绿”字，因为只有“绿”能让人看到颜色、看到春天的变化。这就是有名的“炼字”故事——古代诗人会反复推敲一个字。最后一句问：明月什么时候能照着我回家呢？把思乡之情留在问句里，余味很长。
analysisEn: Wang Anshi’s home was in Jiangning (today’s Nanjing), south of the Yangtze. Here he has moored his boat for the night at Guazhou, on the north bank. The first two lines are about distance: Jingkou and Guazhou are separated only by the river, and Zhongshan, the mountain near his home, is just a few hills further on. Home looks so close — yet he can’t go back. The third line is the famous one. 绿 (lǜ) normally means “green”, but here it is a verb: the spring wind has “greened” the south bank again. Legend says Wang first wrote 到 (“reached”), then tried 过 (“passed”), 入 (“entered”), 满 (“filled”) and about ten other words before settling on 绿, because only “green” lets you actually see spring arriving — the colour spreading along the shore. Chinese teachers tell this story to show what 炼字, “refining a word”, means: poets would weigh a single character again and again. The poem ends with a question: when will the bright moon shine on me as I return home? Leaving the homesickness inside a question makes it linger.
background: Wang Anshi (1021–1086) was a poet and the chief minister behind the Song dynasty’s great reforms. The poem is traditionally dated to 1075, when he was called back to the capital to serve as chief minister again, though some scholars place it at other points in his career.
pronunciation: 一水间：间 本网站按通行读法读 jiān（中间、之间）；也有人认为是“隔开”义，读 jiàn。数重山：数 shù，重 chóng（层），不读 zhòng。照我还：还 huán（回来），不读 hái。泊船：泊 bó。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材（六年级上册）版本。“绿”字的修改过程见于宋代洪迈《容斋续笔》的记载。“春风又绿江南岸”一作“春风自绿江南岸”。

lines.py: jīng kǒu guā zhōu yī shuǐ jiān
lines.lit: Jingkou and Guazhou — one river between them;
lines.en: Only one river lies between Jingkou and Guazhou;

lines.py: zhōng shān zhǐ gé shù chóng shān
lines.lit: Zhongshan is separated by only a few layers of hills.
lines.en: my home on Zhongshan is just a few hills away.

lines.py: chūn fēng yòu lǜ jiāng nán àn
lines.lit: The spring wind again greens the south bank of the river;
lines.en: The spring wind has turned the south bank green again —

lines.py: míng yuè hé shí zhào wǒ huán
lines.lit: When will the bright moon shine on me returning?
lines.en: when will the bright moon light my way home?

words.en: Guazhou, a town on the north bank of the Yangtze
Jingkou, a town on the south bank (today’s Zhenjiang)
a single stretch of water — here the Yangtze

words.note: 重：层。现代汉语“重重”“万重山”。
形容词用作动词，是本诗最有名的“炼字”。
今天仍常用，指长江下游以南的地区。

imagery.name: 长江
imagery.zh: 一条长江把诗人和家乡隔开：近在眼前，却过不去。
imagery.en: The Yangtze separates him from home — so close he can see it, yet he cannot cross.

imagery.name: 春风
imagery.zh: 春风吹绿了江南，春天年年回来，诗人却还不能回家。
imagery.en: The spring wind greens the south bank; spring comes back every year, but he still cannot go home.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 明月照着归人，寄托着回家的盼望。
imagery.en: He hopes the moon will one day light his way home — it carries his longing to return.
